Declare what a recorded scorer measures

Source: R/pair-trajectories.R
comparison_scorer.Rd

A vitals result records a scorer label and, for an ordered factor score, its levels. It does not record a scorer version, and it records no direction for numeric, logical, or character scores. comparison_scorer() declares those facts so pair_trajectories() can decide whether two recorded outcomes came from the same scorer. A declaration is the caller's assertion; scans cannot verify it. A declaration that contradicts the record is an error.

Usage

comparison_scorer(
  scorer,
  version,
  scale = c("binary", "ordered", "numeric"),
  direction = c("higher", "lower"),
  levels = NULL,
  id = scorer
)

Arguments

scorer

The scorer label recorded in trajectory_evaluations()$scorer.

version

The scorer version: any string that changes whenever the scorer's code, prompt, grading model, or rubric changes.

scale

"binary", "ordered", or "numeric".

direction

Whether a "higher" or "lower" value is better. An undeclared ordered factor score is read as "higher", the vitals convention that levels run from worst to best; declare "lower" when a scorer's levels run the other way. The declared levels must still match the recorded level order.

levels

For binary and ordered scales, the possible values from lowest to highest. Not used for a numeric scale.

id

The scorer's identity. Defaults to the recorded label. Supply one shared id when the same scorer was recorded under different labels.

Value

A scans_comparison_scorer value.

Examples

comparison_scorer(
  "detect_exact()",
  version = "vitals-0.4.1",
  scale = "binary",
  direction = "higher",
  levels = c("I", "C")
)
#> $scorer
#> [1] "detect_exact()"
#> 
#> $id
#> [1] "detect_exact()"
#> 
#> $version
#> [1] "vitals-0.4.1"
#> 
#> $scale
#> [1] "binary"
#> 
#> $direction
#> [1] "higher"
#> 
#> $levels
#> [1] "I" "C"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "scans_comparison_scorer"
